data.narrative:
iQPS is a publicly traded Space & Aerospace company founded by Tetsuo Yasaka, Akira Sakurai, and Kunihiro Funakoshi. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector, same-stage public peers: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach, given iQPS's public status and direct comparability to the peer set. The median valuation across these four Space & Aerospace peers is $5.2B, with a range spanning $840M at the low end to $40.0B at the high end. This dispersion reflects heterogeneity in business models and market positioning within the sector. The Public-Comp Anchoring method—which would apply a sector-wide P/S multiple of 27.4x observed across six public Space & Aerospace tickers—cannot be applied due to the absence of iQPS revenue data on file.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $4.4B to $6.0B, centered on the peer median of $5.2B. Key uncertainties include iQPS's relative revenue scale and profitability trajectory versus the peer group, neither of which are specified in available data. The wide dispersion in peer valuations ($840M to $40.0B) indicates that stage and sector affinity alone are insufficient to narrow valuation range; contract value and revenue growth visibility would materially inform positioning within the derived band.
